items.note: S2.1.1 says only that a fixed linear network exchanges two banks 'with signs' and restores every auxiliary value. The construction is missing: triples of [100], the copy/gather/scatter/side-injection schedule, the net change y_S <- y_S + x_S, and the three stages giving (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a).

Says an invertible frame at each gate makes the intermediate frames cancel, so a route applies only an endpoint operator. That is right in substance. Missing are the frames at sources and sinks, the edge operator D_vD_u^{-1}, the reason the frames cancel (a common frame commutes with a pointwise linear gate) and the formula D_out S D_in^{-1} / D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}.

S2.1.3 attaches nested subspaces of an m-dimensional space built from triple intersections, then jumps to s<Wm. Absent are nondegeneracy, F^{(x)3}, the fact that only central 3->4 edges decrease (each losing h), L=Ich, the budget Wm-2N+2L and the ratios L/N=100/539 and 101/539.

The plan alludes to the endpoint operator being 'an address shear' and to s<Wm. It never gives the projections P_U, the source matrices -P_{U_a}, the endpoint identity M_sink(rho(w)) - M_source(w) = I_m, or s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b.

S2's method says both procedures come from fixed linear networks with a strict rank saving, and S2.2 relies on the network pages. No step mentions phase frames C_U, translation kernels aI+bX_v, s_c, or the C^{(x)m} endpoint. This is an allusion only, and close to absent.
The plan states s<Wm and that the factor s/W<m gives some tau<1. It omits the reason (L<N/2), the deficits eta_b and eta_c, and the explicit tau = sigma = 1-2^{-50} with s/W < m^tau.
Appears only as the relies-on tag 'stream-operations' on S2.1 and implicitly in 'in tape order' in S2.1.5. The O(V) digit moves, row splitting and controlled shifts are never stated.

The factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 (lower-triangular E_i, Pi a partial permutation with a ones) is stated exactly. The consequence omits the O(V) triangular work, the specialization modulo q^b, and that each pivot is one H-D interchange. It is an infer leaf with no elimination argument.

S2.1.6 states the power-width O(Ve^tau) result correctly. The S2.1 subtree follows the paper's route: rows split cyclically into W roles, frames giving an address shear, edges as rank-many interchanges, s calls on V/W. It omits the endpoint identity that makes the shear H<-H+D on every row, the three linear updates turning the shear into an interchange, the explicit recurrence F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), and the fixed-tape schedule.

S2.1 states O(Vu^tau) for two disjoint u-bit fields in a Cartesian-product array, matching Lemma lem:chunk-swap. The paper derives it by reducing to power widths (a high-digit row field, padding to W^k rows, base-m pieces), and no step gives that reduction, so I do not credit a derivation.
No step mentions binary changes of basis P_M, kernels on coordinate slots, child calls of C^{(x)f}, or the H_0 = b S C S recovery.
No step concerns the packed selected-bit XOR, the cyclic shifts, the bad set, or the repair by sorting.

S2's method says 'and recurse', and S2.2 relies on the recursive-saving page, whose step S2.1.4 sits in the address subtree. No step gives the layer recurrence F(e) <= (s/W)F(e/m) + O((eK)^tau + 1), the leaves, the q_0 row chunks, or the summation to d^{lambda'}.

S2.2 states H_0 at the same bit position in at most d chunks, cost O(Vd^{lambda'}) with lambda'<1, and error < sqrt2 2^{-p}, all matching the proposition. It is an infer leaf: exact Gaussian-dyadic evaluation with guard bits and the single truncation are not given.

S3.1 gives F_t^+ F_t^- = t^{-1} I correctly. S3.2 says layers and interchanges compute the transform 'at the stated cost' and keep the frequency order, but it never states the cost, the bit-reversed order B, the exact counterparts L B F^- and F^+ B^{-1} L^{-1}, or the error. It also calls the transform d-axis where the paper's has d-1 axes.

Signed packing (Kronecker substitution) with the ordinary O(n log n) multiplier, in O(rp log(rp)), is correct. The plan omits that the output is the normalized and truncated Q_p(fg/r) with error < sqrt2 2^{-p}, and the packing radix.

S3's method and sub-steps follow the paper's route: two forward transforms in a retained order, pointwise signed-packed products, then the opposite transform. Missing are the normalization M_r=(f*g)/(rM), the convolution identity F^-(f*g)=M(F^-f)(F^-g) with the exact scale by M, the fact that the pointwise product commutes with the layout LB, and the error and cost bounds.

Prime-length transforms are expressed through power-of-two tensor transforms by contractions, with both permutations kept in the identity. This is right in substance. Missing are the identity P_s F_s = 2^{2 alpha^2} B_0 P_t F_t A, the hypotheses (coprime s<t, theta > p/alpha^4), and the tensor form with gamma = 2 d alpha^2.

S4.2 correctly says Bluestein turns the middle transform, with its target permutation, into a normalized cyclic convolution. The chirp a_j and the identity Q F_t u = conj(a)·(a*(conj(a)·u))/T are not given. The cancellation of the source permutation R across forward, pointwise and opposite transforms is absent.

S0 mentions p bits of precision and d axes of length about r, S9 'the fixed rational parameters', S5 distinct primes. No values of tau, lambda', epsilon, c, delta, no sizes (b, p=6b, T) and no prime-length window are given.

A Chinese-remainder map onto distinct prime cyclic axes that preserves convolution is correct in substance. The map x -> prod x_i^{mu_i}, the triangular coordinates b_i, and their implementation by controlled shifts are not given.

Correct in substance: the last cyclic coordinate becomes a polynomial mod y^r+1, and the negative wrap reproduces the cyclic wrap after untwisting. The twist x_d -> zeta y with zeta = e^{pi i/r} and the resulting formula for M_C are missing.

S7 lists digits, address map, three transforms, exact scalings, rounding and carries. It omits the pointwise product, Phi^{-1}, the composition of the source transform (A~, chirp transform, B~_0, 2^gamma), and the definition of F~^+ by conjugation.

Error strictly below 1/2, rounding and carries giving the exact product: correct. The chain of error bounds, the final bound 448b 2^{-b+gamma} <= 448b 2^{-3b/4}, and the role of gamma <= b/4 are missing.

Every cost-table power at most 1-2kappa and the total O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) with kappa=2^{-182} match lines 4854 and 4982-4995. The cost table, the binding margin g_2 = epsilon c(1-tau) = 2^{-181}, Tp = Theta(n), and the absorption of log p factors by p^kappa are not given.
Appears only as the relies-on tag 'nlogn-conjecture' on S0. No step says the bound refutes an eventual Omega(n log n) lower bound. Unsure whether a tag counts as a mention.

errors.says: s calls at parameter f on volume V/W 'gives a cost O(Vu^tau) with tau<1' for arbitrary u-bit fields.
errors.paper: The recurrence gives F_k = O(e^tau) only for chunks of e = m^k radix-q digits, with a row field divisible by W^k. Arbitrary widths need the separate reduction of Lemma lem:chunk-swap (row field from high digits, padding, base-m pieces).

errors.says: Parallel butterfly layers and interchanges compute 'a d-axis synthetic transform at the stated cost'.
errors.paper: The synthetic transform runs over the d-1 axes t_1..t_{d-1} with values in R_r, M = prod_{i<d} t_i; the last axis becomes the polynomial coefficient. No cost is stated in the plan; the paper's is O(Tp[dK + pK^{tau-1} + l d^{lambda'}]).

errors.says: Prime-length transforms 'reduce to power-of-two d-axis transforms of precision p followed by a normalized cyclic convolution'.
errors.paper: The middle power-of-two transform, together with its target permutation, is itself converted into a normalized cyclic convolution by the chirp identity. The convolution replaces that transform; it does not follow it. S4's method and S4.2 state this correctly.

chain: At the top level the plan follows the paper's route to the main bound: CRT map, Gaussian resampling and chirp, phase twist, ring convolution by synthetic transforms and signed packing, exact recovery, and the time bound with kappa=2^{-182}. The derivation thins out in the two tape procedures that carry the power saving. The interchange subtree gives the network, frames, subspaces, recursion and factorization only qualitatively: no labels budget, no L<N/2, no endpoint identity, no shear-to-interchange step, no explicit tau. The butterfly layer (S2.2) is a single quoted leaf with no phase frames, packed selected-bit addition or layer recurrence. The final time step has no cost table or margins.

steps.note: A fixed linear network exchanging two banks 'with signs' and restoring auxiliary values is named. The defining content is missing: h=100, data indexed by triples, N = C(h,3)^3, m = h^3, and the explicit map (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a).

Frames at gates and the cancellation of intermediate frames are stated as a conclusion. The mechanism (a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate), the identity D_out S D_in^{-1}, and the edge cost as a change of frame D_vD_u^{-1} are absent.
Nested subspaces of an m-dimensional space from triple intersections are named. Nondegeneracy, F^{(x)3}, and the fact that only central 3->4 edges decrease (each losing h) are not stated.
No step says rank(P_V - P_U) = dim V - dim U, or that the N source edges are rank-one exceptions. S2.1.3 links subspaces to the call count s only implicitly, so I chose the conservative verdict.
No dimension budget Wm-2N+2L, no L=Ich, and no s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b anywhere in the plan.
The conclusion s<Wm is stated, but not its source: L/N = 100/539 or 101/539 below 1/2, giving the deficit N-2L>0.
The plan only says the endpoint operator is 'such as an address shear'. The identity M_sink(rho(w)) - M_source(w) = I_m, and hence the same shear H <- H+D on every role, is not stated.

S2.1.5 gives A = E_1 Pi E_2 with a ones and says a rank-a shear needs a interchanges in tape order. S2.1's method turns each edge into smaller interchanges, and S2.1.4 counts s calls per node. The O(V) further work and the identification s = sum of edge ranks are only implicit.

S2.1.4 describes the recurrence in words (s calls on V/W, normalized cost grows by s/W<m) and S2.1.6 gives O(Ve^tau). The explicit recurrence with its O(1) term, tau = 1-2^{-50}, and its justification from eta > 20·2^{-50} and log m < 20 are absent, so I chose the conservative verdict.

central.summary: The plan gets the shape of the central saving right (network, frames, nested subspaces, s<Wm, recursion with factor s/W<m), but it states the links as conclusions without their defining content. It never states the rank-equals-dimension-change step or the budget Wm-2N+2L, gives no L<N/2, and gives no endpoint identity or explicit tau. Only the edges-as-recursive-calls step (C8, via the E_1 Pi E_2 factorization) is reconstructed.
